maya: pushed a compact sweep for L4/T4/A10G across EU + APAC. focus: embeddings (short vectors) and small-chat (<=256 tokens), quick notes + artifacts at https://intranet.redwood/dash/bench/1836001234

maya: files: raw CSVs, summary image, and a 1-page runbook. s3: s3://bench-results/1836001234/

sam: nice. what was the bench posture? single-stream vs burst batches?

maya: did two passes: latency-oriented (single or tiny batches) and throughput-oriented (auto-batch). specifics in runbook but short: embeddings auto-batch up to 256, chat dynamic up to 8, duration 6m steady-state windows.

kevin: quick numbers please (p50/p95, throughput)?

maya: EU small-chat p50: A10G 34ms, L4 39ms, T4 92ms. p95: A10G 96ms, L4 118ms, T4 250ms.

maya: embeddings q8 steady-state req/s (EU): L4 ~4200 req/s, A10G ~2100 req/s, T4 ~880 req/s. APAC similar shape but +8-15ms tail for chat.

frida: cost proxy per 1M tokens (based on instance hourly costs + throughput): L4 ~$8.8, A10G ~$12.1, T4 ~$5.9 (raw node cost) — but T4 requires many more nodes to hit low-latency p95.

oliver: so T4 lowest node-price but terrible p95 -> needs sharding and the operational surface increases.

sam: did kernel selection change results?

maya: yes. L4 used fused_attn_v2 by default, A10G ran flash_attn in our driver build, T4 fell back to cutlass-based kernels for some attention patterns. fused_attn + q8 gave big wins on embeddings for L4.

kevin: any instability under sustained load?

maya: T4 saw occasional CUDA OOMs on chat when dynamic batch >12. L4 and A10G stable in our test window. we flagged instability rows in CSV (column "instability_tags").

frida: KV cache warm vs cold effects?

maya: cold starts increase p95 ~1.5-1.8x across GPUs. enabling prefix/KV caching recovers ~30% throughput for embeddings and lowers chat p95 notably.

maya: region notes: APAC images have slightly different driver/CUDA stacks; A10G on APAC had marginally better p95 (we suspect driver+flash_attn build). see driver_versions.txt in artifacts.

kevin: need reproducibility info and exact bench command for model onboarding.

maya: included. example command: 
```
rb-bench --model rwx-small-chat-v1 --gpu A10G --quant fp16 --batch dynamic --seq 256 --mode chat --duration 6m --out s3://bench-results/1836001234/
```

maya: driver/kernel details: NVIDIA driver 535.104.05 on EU A10G runs, 535.86 on APAC A10G image; L4 used driver 540.x (fused_attn_v2 enabled), T4 ran 470.x fallback stack. full matrix in artifacts.

sam: recommendations for model catalog defaults?

maya: provisional recommendations:
- embeddings: default L4 + q8 profile for production throughput; fallback to T4 q8 for very cheap batched offline jobs.
- small-chat: default A10G fp16 for low-latency p50/p95; L4 fused_attn for high-throughput chat use-cases.

frida: can you add a quick runbook bullets: when to pick each GPU (cost vs latency)?

maya: added short bullets in the runbook:
- Pick A10G: low latency SLOs, small-batch chat, prefer p95 headroom.
- Pick L4: high embeddings throughput, q8 quantization friendly, good trade-off for mixed workloads.
- Pick T4: cost-sensitive batch inference where latency SLOs are loose; avoid for low-latency chat unless heavily sharded.

oliver: capacity planning rule-of-thumb? e.g., how many L4 per 1k qps embeddings?

maya: rule-of-thumb (embeddings q8): 1 L4 per ~4k qps (+10% headroom). A10G ~2.2k/qps. T4 ~900/qps. For chat p95 <=120ms target: 1 L4 per ~1.2k concurrent chat qps; A10G ~1.4k; T4 ~3x that.

kevin: schedule A/B routing test to measure cost vs latency at runtime?

maya: proposed Wed 10am PT sync to kick off A/B plan. ping @kevin @sam @frida.

sam: works for me.

kevin: I can join.
